claim: CURE trains general-domain LLMs to self-report claim-level confidence for long-form factual generation via a claim-aware reasoning protocol (<think> then <decompose> stages producing (claim_i, confidence_i) pairs), explicitly motivated by the inadequacy of a single scalar confidence for responses containing many claims of varying uncertainty.
stance_target: sufficiency of scalar (whole-response) confidence for outputs with multiple independently-verifiable sub-units
scope_conditions: long-form factuality generation (biography, open-domain QA), general domain, not code
quoted_support: existing approaches remain limited to a single scalar confidence for the entire response, which is insufficient... where uncertainty varies across individual claims

claim: CURE improves claim-level accuracy by up to 39.9% on Biography generation and achieves a 16.0 percentage-point increase in AUROC on FactBench relative to competitive baselines, while maintaining factual recall.
stance_target: efficacy of claim-level self-expressed confidence training for improving both factuality and calibration/discrimination
scope_conditions: four long-form factuality benchmarks (biography generation, FactBench, etc.), general domain
quoted_support: improving claim-level accuracy by up to 39.9% on Biography generation and achieving a 16.0% increase in AUROC on FactBench

claim: CURE's ground-truth labels for per-claim correctness come from an external fact-verification pipeline (VeriScore, retrieval-based), not execution or unit tests, distinguishing its label source from DPRC's 'free' execution-derived per-unittest-method labels.
stance_target: differentiation of CURE's labeling mechanism from DPRC's execution-based labeling
scope_conditions: long-form NL factuality claims vs code unit-test requirements
quoted_support: Ground-truth labels for claims come from an EXTERNAL fact-verification pipeline (VeriScore, retrieval-based), not execution -- claims are natural-language factual assertions ('X was born in Y'), not test cases.

claim: CURE is the closest methodological analog to DPRC found in this search: both train the generating LLM itself (not a separate diagnostic model) to self-report structured, sub-response-level confidence via SFT+RL.
stance_target: DPRC's methodological novelty claim (self-expressed, native, structured confidence)
scope_conditions: comparison of self-report training mechanism across domains
quoted_support: confidence IS the coder-analog LLM's OWN self-report, not a separate diagnostic model (matches the proposed paper on this axis)
